title: Science teaching self-reflection | Leave one real decision for students

qcReview.basis: The 14 English item texts and order match the corresponding factor in Kang et al. Appendix B, pp. 510–513. The original study used five frequency positions; methods §3.1 lists only endpoints 1 = rarely and 5 = always. The project preserves numeric 2–4 and the complete-response 1–5 factor mean. No study averages, norms or thresholds are used.

interpretations.headline: Leave one real decision for students
interpretations.summary:
Students compare how two containers keep warm water from cooling. Each group decides how to make the comparison fair, records what happens, and explains which part of the evidence led it to its conclusion. Groups then compare what they would change. The practical becomes an inquiry because the students have something to work out.

This average reflects the opportunities for exploration, reasoned explanation, teamwork and reflection that you report providing. A higher response pattern can describe more reported opportunities. The score alone cannot tell you what students did with them. Choose one moment when learners could make a decision, test an idea, or defend a conclusion.

guidance.text: In one upcoming investigation, leave students a meaningful decision about the question, comparison, or representation of results. Ask them to explain why they chose it and what evidence would challenge the result.
Collect two group explanations. Check whether each group used a specific observation to support its claim, and decide what prompt would help the next discussion.

limitations: Kang, N.-H., Kang, H., Maeng, S., Park, J., & Jeong, E. (2020). Teacher Competency in Competency-Focused Science Teaching in the South Korean Context: Teacher Self-Assessment Instrument Development and Application. Asia-Pacific Science Education, 6(2), 480–513. https://doi.org/10.1163/23641177-BJA10012 (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The project separates each published factor and supplies its own instructions, complete-answer rule and feedback.

This score is the mean of 14 responses, from 1 (rarely) to 5 (always), and requires all 14 answers. It describes self-reported practices and may include judgments about your understanding or effectiveness. It contains no objective performance score, norm, or cross-factor total.

The original study used the full instrument with 210 South Korean primary and secondary science teachers. This research and self-reflection version uses the published English item wording. The project has not obtained the Korean administration form. Separate use of this factor and equivalence to a Chinese version have not been established.
report.disclaimer: For your own professional learning and research reflection as a science teacher. The result supports a conversation about practice and does not establish teaching quality, teacher eligibility, or student outcomes.
